description: The baseline is the average of the group-level averages, with every telescope/weather group counting equally.

b.request: Join signals to their telescopes and observatories using inner joins; calculate the average modulation index and average phase shift for each telescope and weather profile; use the unweighted average of those telescope/weather groups’ average modulation indices as the overall baseline; retain groups whose average modulation index exceeds that baseline; then, for each weather profile, report the unrounded averages of the retained groups’ average modulation indices and average phase shifts, plus their average modulation-index excess over the baseline
b.sql: WITH telescope_weather AS (SELECT t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile, AVG(s.modindex) AS avg_modindex, AVG(s.phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phaseshift FROM signals AS s INNER JOIN telescopes AS t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry INNER JOIN observatories AS o ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(avg_modindex) AS overall_avg_modindex FROM telescope_weather) SELECT tw.weathprofile, AVG(tw.avg_modindex) AS avg_modindex, AVG(tw.avg_phaseshift) AS avg_phaseshift, AVG(tw.avg_modindex - b.overall_avg_modindex) AS avg_modindex_excess FROM telescope_weather AS tw CROSS JOIN baseline AS b WHERE tw.avg_modindex > b.overall_avg_modindex GROUP BY tw.weathprofile

a.request: Link each signal to its telescope and that telescope's observatory, dropping signals that don't match. For each telescope and weather profile (`weathprofile`), work out the average modulation index and the average phase shift. Keep the telescope/weather groups whose average modulation index is above the mean of those group averages, with each group counting equally. Then for each weather profile, return the weather profile, the average of the kept groups' average modulation index, the average of their average phase shift, and the average amount by which their modulation index is above that baseline. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH telescope_weather AS (SELECT t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile, AVG(s.modindex) AS avg_modindex, AVG(s.phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phaseshiftdeg FROM signals AS s INNER JOIN telescopes AS t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry INNER JOIN observatories AS o ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(avg_modindex) AS mean_group_modindex FROM telescope_weather) SELECT tw.weathprofile, AVG(tw.avg_modindex) AS avg_modindex, AVG(tw.avg_phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phaseshiftdeg, AVG(tw.avg_modindex - b.mean_group_modindex) AS avg_modindex_above_baseline FROM telescope_weather AS tw CROSS JOIN baseline AS b WHERE tw.avg_modindex > b.mean_group_modindex GROUP BY tw.weathprofile;

c.request: Linking signals to their telescopes and observatories (signals that don't match are dropped), find the average modulation index and average phase shift for each telescope and weather profile (`weathprofile`). Keep the telescope/weather groups whose modulation index is above the overall average modulation index. Then, per weather profile, show the average modulation index and average phase shift of those groups, and how far above the overall average they are on average. Don't round anything. The baseline is the average of the group-level averages, with every telescope/weather group counting equally.
c.sql: WITH telescope_weather AS (SELECT t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile, AVG(s.modindex) AS avg_modulation_index, AVG(s.phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phase_shift FROM signals AS s JOIN telescopes AS t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry JOIN observatories AS o ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(avg_modulation_index) AS overall_avg_modulation_index FROM telescope_weather) SELECT tw.weathprofile, AVG(tw.avg_modulation_index) AS avg_modulation_index, AVG(tw.avg_phase_shift) AS avg_phase_shift, AVG(tw.avg_modulation_index - b.overall_avg_modulation_index) AS avg_above_overall FROM telescope_weather AS tw CROSS JOIN baseline AS b WHERE tw.avg_modulation_index > b.overall_avg_modulation_index GROUP BY tw.weathprofile

d.request: Link signals to their telescopes and observatories, dropping signals without a match. For each telescope and `weathprofile` group, calculate the average modulation index and average phase shift. Use the average of the group-level modulation index averages, with every telescope/weather group weighted equally, as the overall baseline. Keep only groups above that baseline. Then, for each weather profile, show the average modulation index and average phase shift of the retained groups, plus their average amount above the baseline. Do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH telescope_weather AS (SELECT t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile, AVG(s.modindex) AS avg_modindex, AVG(s.phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phaseshiftdeg FROM signals AS s JOIN telescopes AS t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry JOIN observatories AS o ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY t.telescregistry, o.weathprofile), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(avg_modindex) AS overall_avg_modindex FROM telescope_weather) SELECT tw.weathprofile, AVG(tw.avg_modindex) AS avg_modindex, AVG(tw.avg_phaseshiftdeg) AS avg_phaseshiftdeg, AVG(tw.avg_modindex - b.overall_avg_modindex) AS avg_above_baseline FROM telescope_weather AS tw CROSS JOIN baseline AS b WHERE tw.avg_modindex > b.overall_avg_modindex GROUP BY tw.weathprofile
